title: The histories that became infrastructure

whole_book_review: Sequential chapter review completed for the saved draft and recorded claims; final cross-book continuity, contemporary refresh and whole-book completion audit remain required. Separate Chapter 3 technical-source queue is not resolved by this review.

historical_scale_revision.scope: Earlier targeted historical-scale revision, subsequently included in the complete sequential chapter review recorded in sequential_review.
historical_scale_revision.boundary: No inevitable historical decline, finite-budget diagnosis of any actual market, independent proof/priority certification, or automatic policy/liability inference.

sequential_review.method: Complete body and all notes read in order after Chapter 3 and after targeted scale revision; revised passages checked in their surrounding sections. Existing source-specific boundaries retained; new facts checked against identified primary passages.
findings: Removed narrator instructions and repeated generic supplier explanations from Bell opening and middle.
Sony technical learning and failed radio casing supply an actual outside-development sequence, explicitly preceding 1956.
Hush-A-Phone waiting times, permission asymmetry and free-hand comparison make timing and evaluation tangible; unresolved legal question distinguished from holding.
Bardeen's failed field-effect proposal supplies a concrete internal discovery path; productive integration retained.
Carterfone reasonable revised standards and owner obligations make interoperability costs and continued development concrete.
Smith/steel/Anderson historical extension remains conditional; no uniform old-market freedom, historical theorem or real-market finite-budget claim.
1952 sharing/1956 decree/1968 attachment chronology, sectoral contrast, disputed QWERTY, Hayek, Merton, Arthur, Alchian and van de Rijt credit retained.
Access to existing information versus new evidence, informative private tests, replay versus intervention and welfare premises remain distinct.
